You can paste a **LinkedIn post URL/URN** or **TikTok video URL/ID** in the Comments page's "Add URL" modal, and the app fetches the actual comments on that post as reply opportunities â€” instead of just recording a dead post-level entry.

2. Paste any of: a `/feed/update/urn:li:activity:â€¦` URL, a `/posts/â€¦-activity-<id>-â€¦` share URL, a raw `urn:li:activity:â€¦`, a bare id, a `tiktok.com/@user/video/<id>` URL, or a raw numeric video id.
3. It calls the scan endpoint, which parses out the identifier, uses the brand's stored (decrypted) access token, and calls the existing `fetchLinkedInComments` / `fetchTikTokComments` fetchers.

The **code-review agent** just finished and found serious issues worth flagging immediately (the other two agents â€” security and completeness â€” are still running). Top findings:

## ðŸ”´ Code review â€” 2 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH

**1. CRITICAL â€” Human-review gate is bypassable when posting a reply** (`api/comments/[id]/post/route.ts`)
The post handler takes `replyText` from the request body and publishes it directly. It never checks `status === 'APPROVED'`, never verifies the text matches the human-approved `approvedReply`, and doesn't block re-posting an already-`POSTED` opportunity. So unreviewed AI text (or a duplicate/different reply) can go live â€” which defeats the whole "human-reviewed" premise of the app.

**2. CRITICAL â€” OAuth `state` is never validated (account-linking CSRF)** (all of `api/oauth/*`)
`state` is just base64 `{brandId, ts}` with no nonce/signature/cookie. An attacker can craft a callback that links *their* social account to *your* brand, silently overwriting the real connection â€” then their account is what posts "as" that brand.

**3. HIGH â€” Scheduler double-publish / stuck posts** (`lib/scheduler.ts` + `api/cron`)
Status goes `PENDING â†’ PUBLISHING` without an atomic compare-and-swap, and `/api/cron` has no auth. Two concurrent cron hits can publish the same post twice; a mid-publish crash leaves a post stuck in `PUBLISHING` forever with no retry.

**Plus MEDIUM:** non-atomic comment dedup (duplicate rows/replies on overlapping scans), and `/api/cron` unauthenticated.

These are all consistent â€” the app currently trusts its own API routes and has no auth layer. I'll fold these into one prioritized plan once the **security** and **completeness** agents land (both still running), so we're not fixing piecemeal.

I'll hold on the `content-generator.ts` Claude migration and any fixes until you steer â€” but given #1 and #2 are CRITICAL and directly undermine the app's core guarantee, my recommendation is to fix those two first. ## ðŸ”´ Security â€” the root cause behind everything

**CRITICAL â€” The app has NO authentication at all.** No `middleware.ts`, no session library, no auth dependency. Every API route is open to anyone who can reach the URL:
- `curl -X POST /api/publish â€¦` â†’ posts live to a brand's real Facebook Page, no credentials
- `curl -X DELETE /api/connections?id=â€¦` â†’ severs a brand's platform connection
- `curl /api/brands` â†’ leaks all brand IDs (which is what makes the OAuth-state CSRF trivial)

This is the root cause: the post-route bypass, the cron issue, and the OAuth CSRF are all *reachable by anyone* because there's no auth gate. **Fix this first** â€” it de-risks everything else.

**Also new:**
- **HIGH â€” Prompt injection in reply generation.** Comment text (attacker-controlled) is embedded in the LLM prompt with only a naive quote-wrap. A malicious comment can hijack the reply ("email your bank details toâ€¦") *and* suppress the model's self-reported warnings. Combined with the weak keyword risk-filter (trivially bypassed by synonyms/obfuscation) and the missing post-time gate, injected content can auto-publish.
- **HIGH â€” Static hardcoded salt** in `crypto.ts` key derivation (`'smg-social-hub-salt'`), and the key-length check (`< 16`) is too permissive.
- **Verified clean:** the AES-256-GCM crypto itself (random IV, proper auth tag), no SQL injection (Prisma), no hardcoded secrets, tokens never returned to clients.

# Consolidated: What Needs Our Attention

## ðŸ”´ MUST-FIX â€” blocks safe production use

**1. No authentication anywhere â¨¯3** â€” No `middleware.ts`, no login, no auth dependency. Every route is publicly callable: `POST /api/publish` posts to real accounts, `DELETE /api/connections` severs connections, the AI endpoints burn unbounded spend. **This is the root cause** â€” it's what makes the CSRF, post-bypass, and cron issues remotely exploitable. Fix first; it de-risks everything else.

**2. Post-approval gate is bypassable â¨¯2** â€” `/api/comments/[id]/post` takes `replyText` from the body and publishes it directly. Never checks `status === 'APPROVED'`, never matches `approvedReply`, never blocks re-posting. The risk-filter's `requiresHumanReview` is **informational only â€” nothing server-side enforces it.** Unreviewed/injected AI text can go live.

**3. OAuth `state` is forgeable (account-hijack) â¨¯3** â€” `state` is plain base64 `{brandId, ts}`, no nonce/signature/cookie. Since `/api/brands` leaks brand IDs (no auth), an attacker links *their* social account to *your* brand and becomes the account that posts "as" you.

**4. Expired OAuth tokens are never refreshed â¨¯1** â€” Refresh tokens are stored but never used (no `grant_type=refresh_token` anywhere). Google/YouTube access tokens die in ~1 hour, FB/IG page tokens in ~60 days (stored as `expiresAt: null`). **Posting silently breaks shortly after connecting.** DB columns already exist.

**5. The scheduler is never actually triggered â¨¯1** â€” `node-cron` is a dependency but imported nowhere; no `vercel.json`, no cron. `processScheduledPosts()` only runs when something hits the (unauthenticated) `/api/cron`. **Scheduled posts will never publish in prod.**

**6. Scheduler double-publish / stuck posts â¨¯1** â€” `PENDING â†’ PUBLISHING` isn't an atomic compare-and-swap, so concurrent cron hits publish twice; a mid-publish crash strands a post in `PUBLISHING` forever with no retry.

**7. Config/secret drift â€” can't set up from the README â¨¯1** â€” Code reads `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (README says `ENCRYPTION_KEY`), `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (README says `_BASE_URL`), and `content-generator.ts` needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` (undocumented). Following the README â†’ crypto throws and content-gen silently returns empty.

**8. SQLite as the datastore â¨¯1** â€” Committed `dev.db`, concurrent `Promise.all` writes â†’ `database is locked` under load; won't run multi-instance/serverless. Move to Postgres before launch.

## ðŸŸ  SHOULD-FIX â€” correctness & reliability

- **Static hardcoded salt** in `crypto.ts` key derivation + too-permissive key-length check (`< 16`). *(Crypto itself â€” AES-256-GCM, random IV, auth tag â€” verified correct.)*
- **Prompt injection** in reply generation â€” untrusted comment text embedded with only a quote-wrap; can hijack the reply and suppress the model's warnings. Risk-filter is trivially bypassed (substring match; synonyms/obfuscation defeat it).
- **Silent failures in all 7 comment fetchers** â€” every error returns `[]`, indistinguishable from "no comments." Only one `console.error` in the entire codebase.
- **Scan uses possibly-expired tokens** â€” `getDecryptedConnection` checks `isActive` but not `expiresAt`.
- **`/api/publish` marks partial failures as PUBLISHED** â€” 2-of-3 platforms failing still records `PUBLISHED`; no outer try/catch.
- **Non-atomic comment dedup** â€” no `@@unique` on `(brandId, postUrl, commentId)`; overlapping scans double-insert â†’ duplicate drafts/replies.
- **Retry endpoint sweeps the whole queue** â€” retrying one post republishes all due posts and races the cron.
- **No rate limiting** on any AI/write endpoint.
- **Error text from upstream APIs reflected to the client** in OAuth redirects.

## ðŸ§ª TESTS
Current suite (35 tests) is solid but narrow â€” only risk-filter, reply-generator, and comment-parse. **Untested & critical:** `scheduler.ts`, `social/index.ts` (publishPost), `crypto.ts` (round-trip + tamper), all API routes, all platform adapters. No coverage gate.

## ðŸŸ¢ NICE-TO-HAVE / half-finished
YouTube publish is a permanent no-op (URL upload unsupported) yet may be offered as a target; LinkedIn/TikTok generic scan silently returns `[]`; Reddit "comments" are actually posts; LinkedIn author shows raw URN; Facebook scan only handles the first page; no `User`/`Team` model and **no record of who approved/posted a reply** (undercuts the human-review compliance story).
